name: OQ-Analyst
short_description: Gold-standard outcome measurement system featuring OQ-45, Y-OQ, and OQ-30 assessments with real-time clinical feedback, expected treatment response algorithms, and 30+ years of validation research.
long_description: OQ-Analyst is the definitive platform for administering and analyzing the Outcome Questionnaire family of assessments, the most extensively validated outcome measures in psychotherapy. Developed by Dr. Michael Lambert at Brigham Young University, the OQ-45 (adult), Y-OQ (youth), and OQ-30 (brief) have been validated in over 200 peer-reviewed studies spanning 30+ years. The system provides real-time clinical feedback including Expected Treatment Response (ETR) algorithms that predict treatment trajectory, red/yellow/green alert signals for patients at risk of treatment failure, and Clinical Support Tools (CST) for struggling cases. OQ-Analyst supports session-by-session administration via paper, kiosk, or online delivery, with instant scoring and visual progress graphs. Research shows that using OQ feedback systems can improve outcomes by 50% and reduce treatment failure rates by 50% compared to treatment-as-usual.
one_liner: Gold-standard OQ-45 outcome measurement with clinical feedback and 30+ years of validation.

faqs.a: The OQ-45 (Outcome Questionnaire-45) is a 45-item self-report measure assessing patient progress across three domains: Symptom Distress, Interpersonal Relations, and Social Role. It's the most validated outcome measure in psychotherapy with 200+ peer-reviewed studies.

faqs.q: How does OQ clinical feedback improve outcomes?
faqs.a: Research shows that providing therapists with real-time OQ feedback improves outcomes by 50% and reduces treatment failure by 50%. The Expected Treatment Response algorithm identifies at-risk patients early.

faqs.q: What is the difference between OQ-45 and OQ-30?
faqs.a: The OQ-45 is the full 45-item assessment taking 5-10 minutes. The OQ-30 is a shorter 30-item version for situations where briefer administration is needed, while maintaining strong psychometric properties.

faqs.q: Is there a version of OQ for children and adolescents?
faqs.a: Yes, the Y-OQ 2.01 (Youth Outcome Questionnaire) is designed for ages 4-17, with parent-report and self-report (ages 12+) versions available.
